The words

Go to dark Gethsemane,
ye that feel the tempter's pow'r;
Your Redeemer's conflict see,
watch with Him one bitter hour,
Turn not from His griefs away;
learn from Jesus Christ to pray.

Follow to the judgment hall,
view the Lord of Life arraigned;
O the wormwood and the gall!
O the pangs His soul sustained!
Shun not suff'ring, shame, or loss;
learn from Christ to bear the cross.

Calv'ry's mournful mountain climb;
there, adoring at His feet,
Mark that miracle of time,
God's own sacrifice complete.
"It is finished!" hear Him cry;
learn from Jesus Christ to die.

Early hasten to the tomb
where they laid His breathless clay;
All is solitude and gloom.
Who has taken Him away?
Christ is ris'n! He meets our eyes;
Savior, teach us so to rise.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Eb and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on d (E♭).
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

The words are by James Montgomery, first published in 1820. The tune, GETHSEMANE, is by Richard Redhead (1853). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.

  • Words (1820): James Montgomery (1771–1854)
  • Music (1853): Richard Redhead (1820–1901)

Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune GETHSEMANE by Richard Redhead (1820–1901); words by James Montgomery (1771–1854). The Open Hymnal Project publishes this hymn as public domain; NoteFusion's engine wrote the solfa from its notes. The melody has not yet been checked against a printed hymn book.

Questions about Go to Dark Gethsemane

What is the doh of Go to Dark Gethsemane?

In this version, in Eb major, doh is Eb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Go to Dark Gethsemane start on?

It starts on d (E♭ in Eb major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

Is Go to Dark Gethsemane in the public domain?

Yes. James Montgomery died in 1854, Richard Redhead died in 1901; the words were first published in 1820 and the music in 1853. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in Nigeria, the UK, the EU and the United States. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
